task: Search for a corrected dual-wield hand-translation model (pivot + shared reach(frame) + angle) to replace the previously falsified rigid single-point-rotation model.
model_formula_note: No deployable closed-form model of the requested shape (hand_absolute = pivot(direction,frame) + reach(frame) * unit_vector(angle(direction,frame)), with angle derived from a formula rather than looked up) survives validation against the CSV ground truth. See honest_assessment and diagnostics below for what was actually tried and measured.
ground_truth: Inputs/DualWeaponAuthored/poses/female-assassin-pair28.csv, 128 attack cells (8 directions x 8 frames x 2 hands), hand_absolute = layer1_absolute(pair_guide) + CSV(x,y) (established CSV-reconstruction rule).

inputs_examined.report_A: tmp/reach_hypothesis_test.py -- direction-invariant reach from body_guide, pair28
inputs_examined.report_B: tools/fit_pivot_offset.py -- general fitted pivot offset, pair28
inputs_examined.report_C: tmp/analyze_pair25.py / tmp/analyze_pair25_dist.py -- pair25 generalization check (raw ACT layers, no CSV correction available)
this_pass_additional_checks: tmp/check_raw_vs_csv.py -- recomputed report C's exact method (raw ACT layer0 vs layer2/3 distance, directions 2/3/4/5 only) on pair28 to see whether pair28's RAW (uncorrected) data shows the same tight invariance report C found for pair25

tmp/check_angle_vs_rotation.py -- tested whether the weapon layer's own baked ActLayer.rotation (already validated to match the CSV's rotation field, established fact) can predict angle-from-pivot-to-hand, i.e. the direction component of the model

tmp/check_body_motion_and_best_case.py -- (1) checked whether body_guide's own frame-to-frame motion within a direction encodes a usable swing-angle signal; (2) computed the best-case error of a reach(frame)-only model given an ORACLE (ground-truth) angle, to isolate how much residual error comes from the magnitude/reach dimension alone

fitted_parameters.note: No parameter set is being proposed for deployment. These are the calibration values that were tested and found insufficient.

previous_falsified_model_baseline.description: rigid single-point rotation of a fixed hilt point, per established facts -- falsified because a rigid rotated vector cannot change magnitude across directions while the CSV's own per-cell magnitude varies 6-30px across the 8 directions at fixed hand+frame.

this_pass_best_case_reach_only_model_wit.description: pivot=body_guide (layer0), reach(frame,hand)=mean(dist across all 8 directions) computed from the CSV itself as a calibration constant, angle=the TRUE ground-truth angle (not predicted -- granted for free to isolate the reach dimension's own error). This is the most favorable possible case for a shared-reach model and is NOT a deployable model (no formula for angle was found -- see below).

rotation_derived.method: csv_angle_conv = ((weapon_layer.rotation + 180) % 360) - 180 (the SAME formula already validated (116/128 exact) against the CSV's own stored per-cell *rotation* field) compared against angle_from_body = atan2(hand_absolute - body_guide) for all 128 cells.
rotation_derived.result: No usable relationship. diff(angle_from_body - rotation_conv) ranges across nearly the full -170..+170 range with no consistent constant or simple linear offset, even within a single frame across directions (e.g. hand0 frame0: diffs 119.8, 119.8, 91.0, 90.6, 88.3, 89.0, 60.2, 60.2 -- no constant, no smooth trend). CONCLUSION: the weapon's own rendering-rotation and the direction from pivot-to-hand are two independently-authored quantities; rotation cannot be used to predict angle.

body_guide_motion_derived.method: Inspected body_guide (layer0) x,y across frames 0-7 for a fixed direction, looking for a frame-to-frame displacement vector that could encode swing phase/angle.
body_guide_motion_derived.result: body_guide does move slightly frame-to-frame (e.g. direction 0: (0,-28)->(2,-28)->(-3,-26)->(-7,-27)->(-7,-27)->(-7,-27)->(-9,-23)->(-7,-22)), but the motion is small (single-digit pixels), non-monotonic, and does not resemble a rotating-arm trajectory. Not pursued further as an angle predictor given the rotation-derived route already failed outright and time did not permit a full regression.

honest_assessment:
No viable simplified hand-translation model was found in this pass. Reports A and B, using the CSV-reconstructed ground truth (the only value established as 'true' -- raw ACT layer2/layer3 are known to drift from it at frames 3-7), both found the reach-from-pivot hypothesis fails as a clean law: Report A found per-frame reach CV across directions ranges 2%-65% (not small), and the angle-from-body vs. direction relationship is non-monotonic with 90-180 degree sign-flipping jumps, ruling out a simple rotating-arm-under-camera-rotation picture. Report B found a general fitted-pivot offset gives only a marginal 5.9% variance reduction for the main hand and a moderate-but-incomplete 33.8% reduction for the off-hand, with residual std still 6.3-9.5px, and -- critically -- the SAME single joint offset is excellent for some frames (var 0.6-1.4) and terrible for others (var 89-259), meaning a fixed pivot only works if it is also allowed to move frame-to-frame, which defeats the point of a 'single fixed pivot' simplification.

Report C appeared to contradict this by finding tight reach-invariance for pair-25, but this pass traced that discrepancy to a methodological difference, not a real pair28-vs-pair25 difference: Report C used RAW (uncorrected) ACT layer offsets for pair25 because no CSV correction exists yet for that in-progress file. When this pass recomputed Report C's exact method (raw layer0-vs-layer2/3 distance, directions 2/3/4/5) on PAIR28's raw ACT data, it ALSO showed tight per-frame invariance (std 0-2.5px against means of 18-65px) -- fully consistent with Report C's pair25 numbers, and NOT consistent with Report A's CSV-corrected numbers for the exact same file (CV 2%-65%, e.g. dagger frame3 dist range 3.6-23.5px). So the raw, human-authored ACT animation genuinely does follow a clean per-frame-shared-reach law across directions (confirmed on two independent pairs), but the CSV corrections that are established as necessary for true rendering accuracy break that clean structure in a direction/frame-specific way. Report C's positive result therefore does not corroborate a model of the quantity that actually needs to be reproduced -- it corroborates the OPPOSITE: that whatever hand-tuned correction process produced the CSV is precisely what destroys the invariant law the raw animation otherwise has.

This pass additionally tried to close the gap in two ways and both failed: (1) the weapon layer's own baked rotation value (already validated to predict the CSV's stored rotation field, 116/128 exact) does NOT predict the angle from pivot to hand -- the discrepancy between the two spans nearly the full -180..+180 range with no constant or trend, so rotation and hand-placement-direction are independently authored quantities. (2) Even granting a model the correct (oracle/ground-truth) angle for every cell and only asking it to predict magnitude via a single per-frame-shared reach constant -- the most favorable possible test of the surviving half of the hypothesis -- mean error is still 7.80px (max 21.95px) across the 128 cells, concentrated in frames 0-2 (the windup portion of the swing, max errors 13-22px) versus near-perfect in frames 3 and 5 (max error under 3px). That confirms Report A's frame-heterogeneity finding quantitatively but also shows that even the best surviving half of the model is not accurate enough or uniform enough to deploy, and it is not even a real model since the angle is not predictable by any formula found.

What the data DOES seem to depend on instead: the raw hand-drawn animation (pre-correction) follows a simple, tight, per-frame-shared-reach-across-directions law -- this is a real, reproducible regularity, confirmed on two different weapon pairs (28: sword+dagger, 25: dagger+dagger). But the corrections captured in the pair28 CSV (required for true in-game accuracy, per established facts about drift at frames 3-7) are direction-and-frame-specific perturbations layered on top of that clean base, and they do not reduce to any of: a rigid single-point rotation (previously falsified), a fixed or fitted-offset pivot with shared reach (marginal/incomplete per Report B and this pass's oracle-angle test), or a rotation-derived angle law (falsified this pass). The likely explanation, echoing Report A's own read, is that the per-direction/per-frame hand placement in the corrected CSV was adjusted by a human animator/tool per-cell (plausibly to fix weapon-sprite clipping/overlap or maintain a specific pixel-level silhouette per camera direction) rather than being generated by any shared kinematic rig. A future investigation could try: (a) regressing the CSV correction (CSV-derived hand position minus the raw-ACT hand position) directly against direction and frame to see if THAT residual/correction term itself has simpler structure than the absolute position does, since the raw base already has a clean law and the correction might be small and more regular than the whole; or (b) checking whether the correction correlates with weapon-sprite bounding-box overlap/collision between the two layers, which would support the clipping-avoidance theory.
comparison_to_previous_falsified_model: The previous rigid-rotation model had mean error 37.5px / max error 106px and was falsified outright (couldn't even match per-cell magnitude in principle). No successor model from this pass reaches deployable accuracy: the best surviving partial idea (shared reach(frame) with a hypothetical, never-found angle predictor) has a theoretical floor of 7.80px mean / 21.95px max error IF the angle were known -- better than the old model's numbers, but that floor is unreachable in practice since no angle-prediction law was found (rotation-derived angle failed completely), so this is not a viable replacement, only a diagnostic upper bound on how good the reach half of the model could ever be.
